Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum 25(OH)D was correlated with lower depressive symptom scores (GDS) across participants.
Sentence: "Serum 25(OH)D correlated positively with MoCA and MMSE scores and inversely with ADL, IADL, and GDS scores."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (GDS)
Population: Hospitalised adults aged 65 or older admitted for comprehensive geriatric assessment in Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Lower serum 25(OH)D levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,438
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Responses

### Response A

 "rationale": "Study A is a single-arm case series of a combined D3/folate/B12 tablet in Parkinson's patients, while Study B is a cross-sectional correlation in hospitalised older adults, so the findings differ in design and cannot truly conflict.",
 "verdict": "genuine",
 "reason": "design_or_bias",

  "outcome_measure"
 ],

}
